contract_tests: paginate(range(1,8), page=2, size=2) returns [3,4] -> test_page_two_size_two_returns_third_and_fourth asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2) == [3, 4] and isinstance(result, list).
paginate(range(1,8), page=1, size=2) returns [1,2] -> test_first_page_returns_first_items asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2].
paginate(range(1,8), page=4, size=2) returns [7] (last partial page) -> test_last_partial_page_returns_remaining_items asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2) == [7].
paginate(range(1,8), page=5, size=2) returns [] (beyond last page) -> test_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 5, 2) == [] and isinstance(result, list).
Empty input returns [] for any valid page/size -> test_empty_input_returns_empty_list asserts paginate([], 1, 2) == [] and paginate([], 3, 5) == [].

Invalid inputs (None-like/non-positive page or size) preserve prior behavior and return [] -> test_invalid_inputs_return_empty_list asserts paginate([1, 2], 0, 2) == [], paginate([1, 2], -1, 2) == [], paginate([1, 2], 1, 0) == [], paginate([1, 2], 1, -3) == [].

Existing public callers of paginate continue to work with one-based page numbers -> test_one_based_page_numbering_offsets_by_page_minus_one asserts paginate(items, 1, 3) == [1, 2, 3], paginate(items, 2, 3) == [4, 5, 6], paginate(items, 3, 3) == [7], paginate(items, 4, 3) == [].

from pagination import paginate


def test_page_two_size_two_returns_third_and_fourth():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_first_page_returns_first_items():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2]


def test_last_partial_page_returns_remaining_items():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2) == [7]


def test_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 5, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_empty_input_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([], 1, 2) == []
    assert paginate([], 3, 5) == []


def test_invalid_inputs_return_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2], 0, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2], -1, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2], 1, 0) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2], 1, -3) == []


def test_one_based_page_numbering_offsets_by_page_minus_one():
    items = list(range(1, 8))
    assert paginate(items, 1, 3) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert paginate(items, 2, 3) == [4, 5, 6]
    assert paginate(items, 3, 3) == [7]
    assert paginate(items, 4, 3) == []

patches.rationale: The bug is that `start = page * page_size` treats page as zero-based, so page=2, size=2 starts at index 4 returning [5,6] instead of [3,4]. Fix: `start = (page - 1) * page_size`. The guard `page < 1 or page_size < 1` already preserves empty/invalid inputs returning [], and slicing beyond the end naturally returns [] for pages past the last page. Existing test `paginate([], 1, 2) == []` and `paginate([1, 2], 0, 2) == []` still pass. Add a new regression test file covering the one-based contract.
